newsitem.title: UK: Manchester Utd shares leap on bid talk.
newsitem.headline: Manchester Utd shares leap on bid talk.

text.p: Shares in British football league champions Manchester United jumped on Friday amid talk of a possible bid for the club, traders said.
Reports in the Times newspaper said a number of companies, including Granada and Whitbread had expressd a strong interest in buying United.
In pre-market trading, the shares spiked up to a record high of 500p before easing back to be up 24p at 476-1/2p.

The Times said a bid was likely to value United at more than 350 million stg. The club is said to have turned down a 300 million stg offer -- around 480p per share -- earlier this year from video and publishing group VCI Plc.
One attraction of the Club to bidders is the opportunities afforded by pay-per-view television which, say analysts, could dwarf current income from even the current BSkyB deal.

"You can come up with some very fancy numbers, given that they claim there are something like 200 million fans worldwide. You don't need to sell too much to too many to get some numbers which are very, very good indeed," said one industry analyst.

Last week, the club reported pre-tax profits of 15.40 million stg, down from the previous year's 20 million stg after falls in income from player transfers and a reduction in spectator capacity for rebuilding of the North stand.
Such figures are likely to pale in comparison to the money available from pay-per-view and whether the United board would accept a bid ahead of the potential bonanza is questionable.
"The numbers being chucked around about TV are very big and people shouldn't convince themselves that the big numbers aren't feasible: they are," said Vinay Bedi of Wise Speke.
"They might not be quite as big as they think but we are certainly talking multiples of current revenues."
